title: Hotfix: disable B200 experimental hardware profile in eu-west pool
author: Irene Choi
release_notes: Mitigation: EU-West B200 pool will not select the experimental B200 hardware tuning profile by default; nodes fall back to standard (non-profile / H100-aligned baseline) scheduling + kernel heuristics until the regression is triaged.
body: Context: During perf-canary + early staged rollout of the B200 experimental tuning profile, eu-west/b200-dedicated showed a repeatable p95 latency regression and elevated retry rate on streaming chat workloads. We are disabling the experimental profile selection in this pool as an immediate mitigation while Kernels/Scheduling dig into root cause. Incident linkage: Slack thread `#incidents` ts=1764395502 ("canary-regression-b200-eu-west-disable-request") and internal follow-up from SRE in `#eng-sre` (rollback criteria / comms). What this changes: (1) Forces `b200_experimental_profile_enabled=false` at the eu-west pool override layer. (2) Adds an explicit allowlist entry so other pools remain unaffected (do not globally disable B200 experimental). (3) Adds a startup log line when pool-level override disables a detected B200 profile, so oncall can quickly confirm effective config. (4) Updates the oncall mitigation playbook snippet (runbook link) with the exact toggle and expected runtime log/metric changes. Scope / safety: This is a hotfix limited to eu-west pool config + a small guardrail in selection logic to emit a structured reason tag. No schema changes. No behavior change for H100/L40S. Testing: Unit tests for override precedence are already present; this adds one focused regression test for "pool override disables experimental profile". CI ran full runtime unit/integration suite on the release branch. Rollout plan: Merge to release/runtime-1.18, deploy to eu-west canary pool first (10% of nodes), verify `runtime_profile_selected` metric drops the `b200-experimental/*` label to `none` or `default` and p95 returns to baseline, then expand to 100% of eu-west/b200-dedicated. Follow-ups: (a) root-cause analysis in ENG-4826 with perf traces and scheduler fairness knobs; (b) tighten perf-canary thresholds to reduce noise but keep this regression class caught; (c) ensure docs for B200 profile reference includes explicit maturity + region gating language.

conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please make sure this is pool-scoped only. We still want experimental enabled in the us-east sandbox pool for debugging. Also add a log/metric reason so oncall can confirm the override is active without SSHing.
Irene Choi (author): Yep — pool override only. I added a structured log line `profile_selection_override_reason=pool_disable_experimental` and an integration test to lock behavior.
Benji Okafor: Can you confirm precedence order? We should be disabling before hardware detection chooses the B200 profile, otherwise we might still end up applying partial defaults.

Irene Choi (author): Precedence is: explicit per-deployment override > pool override > fleet default > auto-detect. The disable happens after detection but before applying any knob set; the log shows detected SKU + suppressed profile name + override source.
Hiro Tanaka: Any chance this masks a kernel selection mismatch that we should keep visible? I'd prefer we keep the metric label for "detected b200" even if profile is suppressed.

Irene Choi (author): We keep `gpu_sku=b200` and emit `profile_selected=default` plus `profile_override_source=pool` and `profile_override_reason=disable_experimental` so we can still segment eu-west B200 performance while profile is off.
Neha Kapoor (SRE sponsor): Add rollback criteria in the PR description (what metrics and thresholds) and ensure docs mention expected impact (p95 drop back, retries normalize).
Irene Choi (author): Added rollout verification bullets + updated the mitigation runbook snippet with exact dashboards to check.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approved. This is the least risky mitigation; we can re-enable once ENG-4826 has a validated fix.
Sean Gallagher: Approved. Please ping #eng-oncall once the canary deploy is complete.
